short: A highly successful American air supremacy fighter with an undefeated combat record.
full:
The McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle entered operational service with the United States Air Force in January 1976. Developed in response to the Vietnam War's lessons on aerial combat and the emergence of the Soviet MiG-25, it was designed specifically for air superiority. Its powerful twin engines, advanced radar, and low wing loading gave it unprecedented maneuverability and acceleration.

The Eagle proved exceptionally lethal in combat, achieving over a hundred aerial victories with zero losses in dogfights, primarily flown by Israeli and American forces. Its success spawned the F-15E Strike Eagle dual-role variant, and the airframe remains a cornerstone of Western air power more than four decades after its introduction.
